title: Bispecific antibody-antigen complex structures reveal activity enhancement by domain rearrangement
one_line: Structural determination of bispecific antibody-antigen complexes showing that rearrangement of antibody domains upon dual antigen engagement underlies enhanced activity.
key_claims: Structures of bispecific antibodies bound to their antigens were solved, revealing the geometry of simultaneous dual-target engagement.
Domain rearrangement within the bispecific format, rather than affinity changes alone, is proposed to account for activity enhancement.
Format and domain arrangement are presented as engineerable determinants of bispecific antibody potency.
The show notes provide only the DOI; no supporting numerical values were available in the episode material.
limitations: No quantitative data (affinities, resolutions, potency values) were available from the episode material, so claims are recorded qualitatively only.
Structural snapshots of complexes do not by themselves demonstrate the causal link between domain rearrangement and functional activity in cells or in vivo.
Authors' own stated limitations were not captured in the published show notes.
open_questions: Do engineered variants that lock or block the observed domain rearrangement lose the activity enhancement, isolating rearrangement as the causal mechanism?
Does the rearrangement-activity relationship generalise across other bispecific formats and target pairs?
How does domain rearrangement translate into cell-based potency and in vivo efficacy?
